Your next alarm (%1$s) is not registered as an alarm clock with Android: the system does not know about it, so the phone may not wake up for it. Open the app to register it again, or re-save the alarm.

WakeNudge expects its next alarm at %1$s, but Android has %2$s. The system does not know about your next alarm, so the phone may not wake up for it. Open the app to register it again, or re-save the alarm.
Notification permission is denied. Alarms still sound, but the full-screen alarm screen and the notification with Snooze and Dismiss cannot appear.
Notifications for WakeNudge are switched off in Android settings. Alarms still sound, but the full-screen alarm screen and the notification with Snooze and Dismiss cannot appear.
The alarm notification channel does not exist yet. Open the app once so it can be created.
The alarm notification channel is blocked, so the alarm screen cannot be shown. Allow it and set its importance to Urgent.

The alarm notification channel was set below Urgent. Android may then show a quiet notification instead of the full-screen alarm screen. The sound itself is played by WakeNudge, so this does not mute alarms.
The \"Alarm sound backup\" notifications are switched off. They are the alarm\'s last resort when Android will not let WakeNudge start its alarm service; switch them back on.
Set to Urgent, so the alarm screen can open over the lock screen.
Granted automatically on this version of Android.
Android 14 and later lets you revoke full-screen alerts. Without them the alarm screen does not open over the lock screen. The sound and the notification still appear.

On this version of Android the alarms themselves need \"Alarms & reminders\". It is switched off, so WakeNudge can only ask for an approximate wake-up, which Android may deliver up to an hour late. Allow it for WakeNudge.
Exact scheduling is not allowed. Alarms use Android\'s alarm-clock channel and are not affected, but timers, the sunrise glow and \"alarm in 30 minutes\" reminders can arrive late.
WakeNudge is exempt from battery optimization.
Android may delay WakeNudge\'s background work to save battery. Alarm-clock alarms are exempt from Doze, so this rarely matters on its own, but an exemption helps timers, reminders and follow-ups.
Your phone\'s maker is known for stopping background apps. Exempt WakeNudge from battery optimization and check the manufacturer-specific advice below.
Android treats WakeNudge as an app in regular use.

Android considers WakeNudge rarely used (the \"Rare\" bucket) and limits its background work. Alarm-clock alarms are exempt, but timers and reminders can be delayed. Opening the app or exempting it from battery optimization moves it up.

Android has put WakeNudge in its most restricted standby bucket, which sharply limits background work. Alarm-clock alarms are exempt, but timers and reminders can be delayed. Opening the app or exempting it from battery optimization moves it up.
Background activity is restricted for WakeNudge. Android may stop an alarm from starting its sound service. Under Battery in the app settings, choose Unrestricted (or at least Optimized).
Not restricted.
Do Not Disturb is off.
Do Not Disturb is set to Alarms only, which lets alarms through.
Do Not Disturb is in Priority only mode and allows alarms.
Do Not Disturb is on and its settings do not allow alarms, so your alarm would be silent. Turn on Alarms under its priority exceptions.

Do Not Disturb is on, and the schedule or mode that turned it on (Bedtime, Sleeping and the like) does not allow alarms: Android has muted the alarm sound, so your alarm would be silent. Allow alarms in that mode\'s settings.
Do Not Disturb is set to Total silence, which silences alarms too. Switch it to Alarms only or turn it off.
Android did not report the Do Not Disturb state.
This device has a fixed volume; the system decides how loud alarms are.
The alarm volume is at %1$d%%.

The alarm volume is only %1$d%%. WakeNudge raises it when an alarm rings, and alarms with their own volume level are unaffected, but alarms set to \"system volume\" would be quiet. Raise it to be safe.
The alarm volume is at zero. WakeNudge raises it itself when an alarm rings, but if Android refuses the change the alarm would be silent. Raise the alarm volume to be safe.
The ringer is on.
The phone is on silent or vibrate. Alarms still ring: their volume is separate from the ringer.
No headphones or Bluetooth audio are connected. Alarms play from the phone speaker.
Connected: %1$s. Your setting plays alarms through the phone speaker even then, so they can still wake you. The hearing-safety cap only applies if you route alarms to headphones.

Connected: %1$s. Alarms follow the system output, so they play in the headphones, capped at %2$d%% to protect your hearing. That may be too quiet to wake you; consider routing alarms to the phone speaker.

Connected: %1$s. Alarms follow the system output and the hearing-safety cap is off, so an alarm plays at full volume directly in your ears. Consider routing alarms to the phone speaker or turning the cap on.
Date, time and time zone are set automatically.
Automatic date and time, or automatic time zone, is switched off. Alarms ring at wall-clock times, so a drifting clock or a wrong time zone moves them.
Alarms and settings are kept in device-protected storage, so alarms ring after a restart even before you unlock the phone for the first time.
Alarm data is not in device-protected storage, so alarms may not ring after a restart until you unlock the phone.
Alarms are switched on, but the scheduler has not registered anything yet. Open the app so it can.
The scheduler has not run yet, and there are no alarms to register.
All alarms were last re-registered on %1$s (%2$s). Reason: %3$s.
No alarm has rung on this device yet.
The last alarm rang on %1$s (%2$s).
The watchdog re-registers all alarms about every six hours as a safety net. It has not had its first turn yet.
The watchdog last ran %1$s. It re-registers all alarms about every six hours as a safety net.
The watchdog last ran %1$s, but it should run about every six hours. Android or the phone maker may be stopping WakeNudge\'s background work.
The watchdog has never run although alarms were registered long ago. Android or the phone maker may be stopping WakeNudge\'s background work.
The alarm sound service has started whenever it was needed.
Android refused to start the alarm sound service: %1$s. WakeNudge then falls back to a plain notification. Check battery and background restrictions.
A text-to-speech engine is installed for voice announcements.
Some alarms announce the time, but no text-to-speech engine is installed, so nothing will be spoken. The alarm itself still rings.
The vibration motor is available.
Some alarms vibrate, but this device has no vibration motor, so that setting has no effect.

Xiaomi, Redmi and POCO phones close background apps aggressively. Open the app info for WakeNudge and turn on Autostart, set Battery saver to \"No restrictions\", and lock the app in the recent-apps screen so it is not swiped away. Menu names vary between MIUI and HyperOS versions.

Huawei and Honor phones manage app launches themselves. In Battery settings open App launch, switch WakeNudge to \"Manage manually\" and allow auto-launch, secondary launch and running in the background. Menu names vary between versions.

OnePlus phones can put apps to sleep. In the app info for WakeNudge allow background activity and unrestricted battery use, turn off battery optimization for it, and lock it in the recent-apps screen. Menu names vary between OxygenOS versions.

OPPO and realme phones can stop apps in the background. In the app info for WakeNudge allow auto-launch and background activity, set battery use to unrestricted, and lock the app in the recent-apps screen. Menu names vary between ColorOS and realme UI versions.

vivo phones limit background apps. Allow WakeNudge to start automatically, and under background power consumption choose \"Allow high background power consumption\" (or the nearest equivalent). Menu names vary between Funtouch OS and OriginOS versions.

Samsung\'s battery settings can put apps to sleep. Under Battery, then Background usage limits, make sure WakeNudge is not listed under Sleeping apps or Deep sleeping apps, and add it to Never sleeping apps. Menu names vary between One UI versions.
ASUS phones can block background apps. In Mobile Manager allow WakeNudge to start automatically, and lock it in the recent-apps screen. Menu names vary between ZenUI versions.
Meizu phones restrict background apps. In Phone Manager allow WakeNudge to run in the background and to start automatically. Menu names vary between Flyme versions.

HMD and Nokia phones follow standard Android battery management. Exempt WakeNudge from battery optimization and, if the phone has a battery-saver or adaptive-battery option, make sure it does not restrict WakeNudge.
